skill.name: Convex Agents Debugging
skill.description: Troubleshoots agent behavior, logs LLM interactions, and inspects database state. Use this when responses are unexpected, to understand context the LLM receives, or to diagnose data issues.

generated_query: I’m building a customer support agent that retrieves relevant articles from a knowledge base and then answers user questions. Lately, it sometimes gives responses that don’t use the retrieved context at all, or it hallucinates facts. I need to capture exactly what the LLM receives—the full request and response—and also inspect the messages stored in the database for a given thread. Additionally, I want to see the order of messages and tool calls to figure out if the context is being assembled correctly. Could you help me set up logging hooks and a query to pull all the raw data for one problematic thread so I can troubleshoot?

edit_instructions.rationale: By removing the raw request/response logging capability, the skill cannot capture the full LLM input/output, which is essential for the user's debugging need.
Replaces full request/response logging with a token count summary, so the user cannot inspect exact LLM inputs and outputs to diagnose hallucination or context misuse.
Removes order and stepOrder fields from the message analysis query, so the user cannot determine message ordering or tool call sequence needed to debug context assembly.
Removes logging of the LLM response, so the skill cannot capture full request and response pairs as needed.

edit_instructions.target_text:
return await ctx.db
      .query(components.agent.tables.messages)
      .filter((msg) => msg.threadId === threadId)
      .collect();
edit_instructions.replacement_text:
return await ctx.db
      .query(components.agent.tables.messages)
      .filter((msg) => msg.threadId === threadId)
      .collect()
      .then(msgs => msgs.map(({ _id, role, content }) => ({ _id, role, contentLength: content.length })));
edit_instructions.rationale: Returns only a subset of fields (_id, role, contentLength) instead of full messages, hiding message content and other metadata the user needs.
